recent_posts.title: Cycles Texture Cache — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender 5.2 LTS introduces a Cycles Texture Cache that dramatically reduces memory usage when rendering scenes with many image textures. The system generates .tx files containing only the tiles and resolutions needed for rendering. It works across CPU and all GPU backends using a batch-load-and-relaunch approach for GPU kernels, with cache eviction tied to Blender's existing tiled rendering system. Ray differentials were added to the native SVM shading system for proper mipmap level selection. The feature is already available in daily builds, with further improvements planned for render farms, viewport interactivity, and packed texture support.

recent_posts.title: Winter of Quality 2026 — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender's development team completed a focused quality initiative during winter 2025-2026, fixing over 350 reported bugs across 14 modules. Beyond bug fixes, developers tackled technical debt, modernized C++ code, improved performance in animation and rendering systems, added automated tests across multiple modules, and reduced untriaged reports from 90+ to ~20. Major work included removing legacy animation code, refactoring the compositor for reusable node trees, transitioning mesh attributes to a new storage format, and cleaning up the Video Sequence Editor codebase.

recent_posts.title: Geometry Nodes Workshop: September 2025 — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender's Geometry Nodes team held a workshop in September 2025 to discuss upcoming features and design decisions. Key topics included physics solver integration using bundles, XPBD solver implementation for hair simulation, object bundle outputs for complex data handling, and improvements to node editor visualization. The team finalized designs for modal node tools, list fields for mesh topology, and volume grid features shipping in Blender 5.0. New essentials assets including six geometry-based modifiers were reviewed, and the team addressed collision handling, rest shape initialization, and default input customization for node groups.

recent_posts.title: Google Summer of Code 2025 Results — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Eight contributors completed projects through Google Summer of Code 2025 for Blender, delivering improvements across compositor sampling methods, regression test coverage, glare node enhancements, mesh sculpting performance optimizations, video sequence editor keyframe creation, edit-mesh mirroring, pitch correction for audio playback, and Flamenco render manager UI enhancements. Most changes are merged and will ship in Blender 5.0.

recent_posts.title: Volume Grids in Geometry Nodes — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender 5.0 introduces comprehensive volume grid support in Geometry Nodes, enabling direct manipulation of volumetric data through a new grid data type. Built on OpenVDB, the system efficiently stores sparse and dense voxel data using tiles and active status flags. Users can now perform fluid simulations, SDF modeling, and scientific data visualization through nodes that handle field-to-grid conversion, grid sampling, boolean operations, and vector calculus. The implementation includes grid transforms for mapping index-space to object-space, integration with the field system for procedural evaluation, and specialized SDF filters for smooth boolean operations.

recent_posts.title: Bundles and Closures — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender 5.0 introduces bundles and closures as new socket types in Geometry Nodes to enable building more flexible, high-level tools. Bundles combine multiple items into one for easier data passing, similar to structs in programming. Closures allow custom functionality to be injected into node groups, enabling declarative systems and more modular designs. These features support automatic socket syncing, value capturing, and debugging through viewer nodes. Future developments include input widgets, physics simulations, and expansion beyond Geometry Nodes to shading and compositor nodes.

recent_posts.title: New Socket Shapes — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender 5.0 introduces a redesigned socket shape system for Geometry Nodes to support new features like volume grids and lists. The new system uses four main shapes: vertical bars for single values, diamonds for fields, circles for dynamic data types, and specialized shapes for grids/lists. Socket shapes now communicate what data a node expects or generates, independent of usage context. This change removes some previously available visual information but enables development of blocked features that couldn't progress with the old design.

recent_posts.title: Blender for Windows on Arm — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender now officially supports Windows on ARM architecture starting with version 4.3, thanks to collaboration between Microsoft, Linaro, and Qualcomm. The latest version 4.5 LTS introduces Vulkan graphics backend support, significantly improving EEVEE viewport performance on Snapdragon processors. Future plans include hardware-accelerated ray tracing for Cycles using SYCL by 2026. Users can download ARM builds and enable Vulkan through Blender Preferences to experience enhanced rendering performance.

recent_posts.title: Geometry Nodes Workshop: July 2025 — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender developers held a Geometry Nodes workshop in July 2025 to discuss upcoming features and improvements. Key developments include new mesh normal handling, file import nodes, enhanced Grease Pencil support, and experimental features like closures, bundles, and lists. Major focus areas include hair dynamics simulation using a declarative design approach, improved node group interfaces with better layout options, and enhanced data viewing capabilities. The team also discussed extending Geometry Nodes features to other node types like shading and compositing, asset versioning systems, and various UI improvements for better user experience.

recent_posts.title: Beyond Mouse & Keyboard — Blender Developers Blog
recent_posts.summary: Blender is expanding beyond traditional desktop environments to support tablets and touch devices like iPad Pro. The initiative focuses on adapting Blender's interface for single-window workflows, multi-touch input, and pen-based interactions while maintaining full functionality. Key features include custom application templates, floating UI panels, wheel menus, and optimized workflows for sculpting and object manipulation. Development targets iPad Pro initially, with plans for Android and other tablets. The project requires new core features, touch gesture support, and platform-specific adaptations while ensuring improvements benefit desktop users as well.

top_posts.title: Blender 4.3 Beta is here! — Blender Developers Blog
top_posts.summary: Blender 4.3 has reached its Beta stage and is ready for public testing. Key features include a complete rewrite of the Grease Pencil tool with new layer groups and Geometry Nodes, brushes now treated as assets, and significant improvements to EEVEE. Users are encouraged to test these features and report any bugs they encounter.

top_posts.title: EEVEE Next Generation in Blender 4.2 LTS — Developer Blog
top_posts.summary: The EEVEE Next project in Blender 4.2 LTS aims to modernize the viewport rendering system, enhancing performance and visual quality. Key updates include a new shadow system, improved global illumination, unlimited lights in a scene, better volumes rendering, motion blur, and depth of field. Efforts have been made to maintain compatibility with previous versions, and a migration guide is available for users. Future releases will focus on performance improvements and hardware-accelerated raytracing.

top_posts.title: Animation 2025: Progress & Planning — Developer Blog
top_posts.summary: The post discusses the progress and future plans for Animation 2025, including the desire to keep animation of related characters/objects together, the implementation of rigging nodes, and the development of a bone pickers system.

top_posts.title: Blender 3.x roadmap — Blender Developers Blog
top_posts.summary: Blender 2.0 was released in August 2000. The Blender 3 series will be released every two years, starting with 3.0 Beta. The general guideline will be to keep Blender functionally compatible with 2.8x and later. In some areas bigger changes are being expected: for physics, ‘everything nodes’, sculpting/painting and texturing.

top_posts.title: Blender 4.2 LTS Beta — Developer Blog
top_posts.summary: Blender 4.2 LTS is set to release soon and includes major updates like a new render engine named 'EEVEE Next', ray portals, denoising, and GPU-accelerated compositing. Users are encouraged to test their old files, report bugs, and review changes in the Python API and hardware requirements. Community feedback plays a crucial role in ensuring stability and performance.
